final_message:
I implemented `find_overlaps` in `labkit/evals/contamination.py`, and both tests in `tests.test_s3_contamination` pass.

It lowercases and whitespace-splits each training doc and builds one set of all word n-grams. It then returns the indices, in ascending order, of test items that share at least one n-gram with that set. An item with fewer than `n` words has no n-grams, so it never matches.

I also added a `ValueError` for `n < 1`. The docstring doesn't ask for this, so remove it if you'd rather not have it.

@@ -1,7 +1,20 @@
+def _ngrams(text, n):
+    words = text.lower().split()
+    return {tuple(words[i:i + n]) for i in range(len(words) - n + 1)}
+
+
 def find_overlaps(train_docs, test_items, n=8):
     """Indices of test items that share a word n-gram with any training doc.
 
     Words are whitespace-separated and compared in lower case. An item with
     fewer than `n` words never matches. Return the indices sorted ascending.
     """
-    raise NotImplementedError
+    if n < 1:
+        raise ValueError("n must be >= 1")
+    train_grams = set()
+    for doc in train_docs:
+        train_grams |= _ngrams(doc, n)
+    return [
+        i for i, item in enumerate(test_items)
+        if not _ngrams(item, n).isdisjoint(train_grams)
+    ]
